ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Numb mouth after a cough capsule

An adult with a troublesome dry cough bites a prescribed benzonatate capsule because swallowing pills is difficult. Within minutes, the tongue feels numb and swallowing becomes uncomfortable. Which mechanism most directly explains this new problem?

  1. Local anesthesia of oral sensory nerves
  2. Histamine-mediated gastric acid secretion
  3. Inhibition of pulmonary surfactant synthesis
  4. Activation of central opioid receptors
  5. Suppression of bone marrow precursors
Answer and explanation

Local anesthesia of oral sensory nerves

Released benzonatate anesthetizes oral tissues and can impair protective swallowing.

Option explanations

Local anesthesia of oral sensory nerves: Released benzonatate anesthetizes oral tissues and can impair protective swallowing.

Histamine-mediated gastric acid secretion: Acid secretion does not explain immediate oral numbness.

Inhibition of pulmonary surfactant synthesis: Surfactant changes would affect alveolar stability rather than oral sensation.

Activation of central opioid receptors: Benzonatate acts peripherally and is not an opioid agonist.

Suppression of bone marrow precursors: Marrow suppression cannot produce this immediate local symptom.
